5MgBikgcWnY.title: The first 20 hours -- how to learn anything | Josh Kaufman | TEDxCSU
5MgBikgcWnY.summary: Josh Kaufman's TEDx talk argues that you can reach practical competence in almost any skill with about 20 hours of focused practice, rather than the 10,000 hours often quoted. He describes how becoming a parent led him to rethink how adults learn, and lays out a short method for rapid skill acquisition.
5MgBikgcWnY.why: HN uses it as the standard counterpoint to the 10,000-hour rule and as an encouraging recipe for starting new skills.

quote.text: the threshold for acquiring new skills for personal or professional use is somewhere around 20 hours.

JOLtS4VUcvQ.title: Spinning Levers - How A Transmission Works (1936)
JOLtS4VUcvQ.summary: A 1936 Chevrolet-sponsored film that explains how a car transmission works by treating gears as spinning levers. It uses physical models to make the mechanism clear.
JOLtS4VUcvQ.why: It is held up as a model of clear, well-paced educational film and of the old-era instructional style.

quote.text: The editing, pacing, and style were better.

hlrv7DIHllE.title: College Lecture Series - Neil Postman - "The Surrender of Culture to Technology"
hlrv7DIHllE.summary: Neil Postman's 1997 lecture at College of DuPage, based on his book, argues that Americans treat technology as a national religion and depend on it to solve larger human problems. It includes audience questions.
hlrv7DIHllE.why: HN recommends it to engineers as a skeptical counterweight to technology boosterism, especially for those building AI and consumer tech features.

quote.text: I suggest the people working on those features watch Neil Postman's "The Surrender of Culture to Technology"

K_nnUbX7uuQ.title: The Secrets Of Cornwall - Part 1 - Communications
K_nnUbX7uuQ.summary: A documentary on how Cornwall became a hub for the world's communications, from the first transatlantic radio signal to modern undersea fibre cables. It describes how cable landing stations and the systems are put together.
K_nnUbX7uuQ.why: Recommended as a rare look at the unmarked buildings and infrastructure where undersea cables come ashore.

quote.text: Documentary about the cable landing stations: The Secrets of Cornwall

gQnmP7UD_zk.title: Etching small patterns in Glass
gQnmP7UD_zk.summary: Huygens Optics experiments with etching tiny patterns in glass, covering hydrofluoric acid risks, buffered oxide etch, photoresist and chromium masks, and laser-induced etching. It ends with attempts at microscopic Tesla valves.
gQnmP7UD_zk.why: HN recommends it as a highly informative look at micro-etching glass and the smallest Tesla valves.

quote.text: The video on micro etching glass with HF is highly informative on this post...

vs41JrnGaxc.title: Jonathan Haidt: The moral roots of liberals and conservatives
vs41JrnGaxc.summary: Psychologist Jonathan Haidt presents his moral foundations research in a TED talk. He argues that liberals and conservatives weigh a different set of moral values, which helps explain political divides.
vs41JrnGaxc.why: HN recommends it as an accessible way to understand why people across the political spectrum disagree and to better understand opposing views.

quote.text: Jonathon Haidt has actually done some great scientific work on the real differences between liberals and conservatives.

rwhUpu9MfZ0.title: PAW Patrol's Dark Secret, Explained
rwhUpu9MfZ0.summary: A long video essay by Skip Intro asking what vision of policing the kids' show PAW Patrol suggests. It mixes comedy with serious critique and features guest voices.
rwhUpu9MfZ0.why: Recommended as a funny but serious critique of the show's portrayal of authority and policing.

quote.text: It’s a superb video essay and absolutely worth the watch!

yYTSdlOdkn0.title: Decaf Explained
yYTSdlOdkn0.summary: James Hoffmann explains how decaf coffee is made, how the decaffeination processes differ, and why decaf is roasted and stales differently. He also discusses decaf quality and health questions.
yYTSdlOdkn0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a well-researched overview of decaf processes and quality, and cite it for the claim that decaf stales faster.

quote.text: his video about decaf sold me on the idea

SZazYFchLRI.title: Iannis Xenakis - Metastasis
SZazYFchLRI.summary: A score-following video of Iannis Xenakis's 1950s orchestral piece Metastasis, showing his graphic, mathematically derived notation as the music plays. It is a landmark of post-war modernist composition.
SZazYFchLRI.why: HN uses it as an example of radically different musical notation and as a favorite, if challenging, modernist piece that anticipates sounds like the THX Deep Note.

quote.text: look at the notation for this piece by Iannis Xenakis.

Boi0XEm9-4E.title: Utrecht: Planning for People & Bikes, Not for Cars
Boi0XEm9-4E.summary: Streetfilms shows how Utrecht reduced car traffic in its center by removing roadways, building huge bike parking near the train station, and making cycling transitions safer and easier.
Boi0XEm9-4E.why: HN users cite it as a short, inspiring look at the Dutch approach to bike-friendly urban planning.

quote.text: Shows the fantastic transformation of Utrecht.

by1xpy8ob8E.title: Can A Metal Bowling Ball Survive Inside a Nuclear Explosion?
by1xpy8ob8E.summary: Scott Manley explains the Cold War experiments in which steel and aluminium spheres, known as Lew Allen's Balls, were placed near nuclear detonations. The spheres survived the fireball, and he walks through what the declassified results show.
by1xpy8ob8E.why: Cited as a fun, well-explained account of objects surviving nuclear blasts, relevant to Orion-style and spacecraft survivability discussions.

quote.text: You might also be interested in the story of Lew Allen's Balls

KEkrWRHCDQU.title: HACKERMAN'S HACKING TUTORIALS - How To Hack Time
KEkrWRHCDQU.summary: A comedic Kung Fury spinoff in which Hackerman demonstrates 'hacking' household objects through time. It parodies 1980s hacker tropes.
KEkrWRHCDQU.why: Posted as a joke whenever HN threads touch on hacking or hackers.

Qdplq4cj76I.title: Steve Jobs : Great idea doesn't always translates into great product
Qdplq4cj76I.summary: A six-minute excerpt from Steve Jobs' 1995 Lost Interview on why a great idea does not automatically become a great product. He says ideas change substantially once you actually build them.
Qdplq4cj76I.why: Quoted in threads on engineering and product building to argue that execution matters more than ideas.

quote.text: Steve Jobs on how ideas change when you actually do it

bdwjcayPuag.title: Rheinmetall Air Defence: Ahead - Highly effective, programmable ammunition
bdwjcayPuag.summary: A one-minute Rheinmetall promotional demo of Oerlikon Ahead air burst ammunition, which throws a cloud of sub-projectiles to destroy small air targets.
bdwjcayPuag.why: HN cites it as an example of programmable airburst ammunition used against drones and fast aircraft.

r-V_Z3bD_PA.title: EEVblog #1107 - Shocking 4K BENQ Monitor Problem!
r-V_Z3bD_PA.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog investigates why a 4K BenQ monitor switches itself off, tracing it to static discharge from an office chair. He uses an oscilloscope to examine the static impulses.
r-V_Z3bD_PA.why: Linked whenever someone reports a monitor blacking out from static electricity, as prior art on the same problem.
